newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-County NatWest to sell via Internet. [CORRECTED 01:10 GMT 10/1]
newsitem.headline: RTRS-County NatWest to sell via Internet. [CORRECTED 01:10 GMT 10/1]

text.p: County NatWest Australia Investment Management said on Thursday it will launch low-cost investment products to the retail market via the telephone and Internet.

County NatWest chief executive Nick Birrell told reporters the investment bank would launch three investment fund products -- one for Australian equities, a balanced fund and a enhanced cash product -- through its new website.
Birrell said management fees for the product were 1.3 percent for Australian equity and balanced options and 1.1 percent for the enhanced cash option.

Birrell said there would be no entry or exit fees for redemptions in excess of A$500. County NatWest head of corporate affairs Paul Murphy said these fees compared with establishment fees of up to five percent and ongoing management fees of about two percent on traditional investment products available in the market. (Corrects to make clear fees mentioned are those generally charged in the market, not those specifically charged by County NatWest.)
"We are not aware if any comparable managed fund products available to personal investors that can match these low fee levels," Birrell told reporters.
He said the new products, called COUNTY Direct would operate beside County's existing retail funds management business.
A spokesman for County NatWest told Reuters the COUNTY Direct products could potentially be in competition to its existing retail funds products.
County NatWest has over A$1 billion under management.

"If it takes business away from our existing products then we have to get use to lower fees, but if these products don't take off then we haven't lost anything, so its a win-win situation," the spokesman said.
County NatWest is owned by British banking group National Westminister Bank Plc.
